edition: Hebrew–English column (Literal-Smooth, Rabbinic Priority) of the Saints.Bible Parallel Reader
source_hebrew: Westminster Leningrad Codex (pointed text via Sefaria)

1:14.english: The living creatures darted back and forth like a flash of lightning.
1:14.editorial_note: The Masoretic reading is present where the Old Greek has no corresponding verse. The rare word בָּזָק is understood as a flash of lightning.

10:14.hebrew: וְאַרְבָּעָה פָנִים לְאֶחָד פְּנֵי הָאֶחָד פְּנֵי הַכְּרוּב וּפְנֵי הַשֵּׁנִי פְּנֵי אָדָם וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁי פְּנֵי אַרְיֵה וְהָרְבִיעִי פְּנֵי־נָשֶׁר׃
10:14.english: Each had four faces. The first was the face of a cherub, the second the face of a human, the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle.
10:14.editorial_note: The first face is explicitly a cherub in this passage. Ezekiel 1:10 lists an ox in its corresponding set of faces.

27:31.hebrew: וְהִקְרִיחוּ אֵלַיִךְ קָרְחָה וְחָגְרוּ שַׂקִּים וּבָכוּ אֵלַיִךְ בְּמַר־נֶפֶשׁ מִסְפֵּד מָר׃
27:31.english: They will shave their heads bald for you and wrap themselves in sackcloth. They will weep for you in bitterness of soul and mourn with bitter cries.
27:31.editorial_note: The repeated bitterness and the emphatic Hebrew image of making oneself bald are retained.

32:19.english: Whom do you surpass in beauty? Go down and be laid among the uncircumcised.
32:19.editorial_note: 'Be laid' preserves the passive imperative. The question and commands address Egypt.

33:26.hebrew: עֲמַדְתֶּם עַל־חַרְבְּכֶם עֲשִׂיתֶן תּוֹעֵבָה וְאִישׁ אֶת־אֵשֶׁת רֵעֵהוּ טִמֵּאתֶם וְהָאָרֶץ תִּירָשׁוּ׃
33:26.english: You rely on your sword, you commit abominations, and each of you defiles his neighbor’s wife. Will you then possess the land?
33:26.editorial_note: The pointed text shifts to a feminine plural verb for 'you commit' amid masculine plurals. English plural 'you' conveys the address without supplying a separate subject. The Hebrew singular 'sword' is retained.

40:30.hebrew: וְאֵלַמּוֹת סָבִיב סָבִיב אֹרֶךְ חָמֵשׁ וְעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה וְרֹחַב חָמֵשׁ אַמּוֹת׃
40:30.english: There were porches all around, twenty-five cubits long and five cubits wide.
40:30.editorial_note: The measurements follow the Masoretic Text. 'Porches' matches this archive's architectural terminology in the surrounding verses.

scope: Additional readings keyed by Masoretic reference, separate from the Parallel Reader’s aligned rows. Entries with staging links document the earlier staging capture. New editorial readings were prepared in the GitHub archive.
